questions.question: What does "www" stand for?
questions.fact: The World Wide Web went public in 1991. The first website ever is still online at CERN.

questions.question: Who co-founded Microsoft with Paul Allen?
questions.fact: Bill Gates and Paul Allen founded Microsoft in 1975. Gates was 19 and dropped out of Harvard.

questions.question: Which company makes the iPhone?
questions.fact: The iPhone's name followed Apple's "i" products like the iMac and iPod. Over 2 billion iPhones have been sold.

questions.question: Who founded Facebook?
questions.fact: Facebook started in 2004 as a website for Harvard students, created in Mark Zuckerberg's dorm room.

questions.question: What does "CPU" stand for?
questions.fact: A modern CPU can do billions of calculations every second.

questions.question: What does "USB" stand for?
questions.fact: USB-C plugs can go in either way round, unlike older USB plugs that always seemed to be upside down.

questions.question: Which company owns YouTube?
questions.fact: Google bought YouTube in 2006 for about $1.65 billion. Over 500 hours of video are uploaded every minute.

questions.question: Which company started out as an online bookshop?
questions.fact: Jeff Bezos started Amazon in his garage in 1994. Its first name was going to be "Cadabra".

questions.question: In which year was the first iPhone released?
questions.fact: The first iPhone was presented by Steve Jobs in January 2007 and went on sale that June.

questions.question: What does Wi-Fi let you do?
options: Connect to the internet without cables
questions.fact: "Wi-Fi" isn't short for anything; it was a catchy brand name chosen to sound like "hi-fi".

questions.question: What is the name of Apple's voice assistant?
questions.fact: Siri started as a separate app; Apple bought the company in 2010 and added Siri to the iPhone 4S.

questions.question: What is Amazon's voice assistant called?
questions.fact: Amazon reportedly chose "Alexa" partly because the hard "x" sound is easy for the device to recognise.

questions.question: What does "AI" stand for?
questions.fact: The term "artificial intelligence" was coined by John McCarthy for a 1956 workshop at Dartmouth College.

questions.question: What is HTML used to create?
questions.fact: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language. Tim Berners-Lee created it for the first websites.

questions.question: Which company has developed Android since buying it in 2005?
questions.fact: Android versions used to have dessert names, like Cupcake, KitKat and Oreo, in alphabetical order.

questions.question: How many bits are in a byte?
questions.fact: Half a byte, four bits, is jokingly called a "nibble".

questions.question: What does "PDF" stand for?
questions.fact: PDF was created by Adobe in 1993 so documents would look the same on any computer.

questions.question: What is "spam" in email?
questions.fact: Junk email is called spam after a Monty Python sketch where the word "Spam" is repeated over and over.

questions.question: What was the very first YouTube video about?
questions.fact: The first YouTube video, "Me at the zoo", was uploaded in April 2005 by co-founder Jawed Karim and is 19 seconds long.

questions.question: Which social network was renamed "X"?
questions.fact: Twitter was renamed X in 2023, after being bought by Elon Musk in 2022.

questions.question: Which company makes the PlayStation?
questions.fact: The PlayStation 2 is the best-selling games console ever, with over 150 million sold.

questions.question: What does "GPS" stand for?
questions.fact: GPS needs signals from at least four satellites to work out exactly where you are.

questions.question: Who presented the first iPhone on stage in 2007?
questions.fact: Steve Jobs called the iPhone "an iPod, a phone and an internet communicator" in one device.

questions.question: What is "the cloud" in computing?
options: Services and storage on remote servers
questions.fact: "The cloud" is really just huge buildings full of computers, called data centres.

questions.question: What does "QR" in QR code stand for?
questions.fact: QR codes were invented in Japan in 1994 to track car parts in factories.

questions.question: Which company created Windows?
questions.fact: Windows 1.0 came out in 1985. Before that, most PCs were used by typing commands.

questions.question: Which programming language runs in every web browser?
questions.fact: JavaScript was created in just 10 days in 1995, and despite the name it has little to do with Java.

questions.question: What does a router do?
questions.fact: Switching your router off and on really does fix many problems, by clearing its memory.

questions.question: What does "VPN" stand for?
questions.fact: A VPN hides your connection inside an encrypted "tunnel", often used to stay safe on public Wi-Fi.

questions.question: What does the "s" in "https" stand for?
questions.fact: The little padlock in your browser shows the connection is encrypted with https.

questions.question: Which company makes Galaxy phones?
questions.fact: Samsung started in 1938 as a small trading company selling dried fish and vegetables.

questions.question: What is Google's web browser called?
questions.fact: Chrome launched in 2008 and quickly became the most used browser in the world.

questions.question: Which web browser has a fox in its logo?
questions.fact: "Firefox" is actually a nickname for the red panda, even though the logo looks like a fox.

questions.question: Who is often called the first computer programmer, back in the 1840s?
questions.fact: Ada Lovelace wrote what's considered the first computer program, for Charles Babbage's planned Analytical Engine.

questions.question: Which British mathematician helped crack the Enigma code?
questions.fact: Alan Turing also invented the "Turing test" for whether a machine can seem intelligent.

questions.question: Who invented the World Wide Web?
questions.fact: Tim Berners-Lee invented the web at CERN in 1989 and gave it away free, without a patent.

questions.question: What does "LOL" usually mean in messages?
questions.fact: In Spanish chats people laugh with "jajaja", because the Spanish "j" sounds like an English "h".

questions.question: What is the most used search engine in the world?
questions.fact: Google handles billions of searches every day, so many that "to google" became a verb in dictionaries.

questions.question: The word "emoji" comes from which language?
questions.fact: "Emoji" comes from Japanese "e" (picture) and "moji" (character). It's a coincidence that it sounds like "emotion".

questions.question: Which app is known for disappearing photo messages and a ghost logo?
questions.fact: Snapchat's ghost mascot is called Ghostface Chillah.

questions.question: Which messaging app, owned by Meta, is used by almost everyone in Spain?
questions.fact: WhatsApp was founded in 2009 and bought by Facebook in 2014 for about $19 billion.

questions.question: Which company owns TikTok?
questions.fact: ByteDance is a Chinese company. TikTok is called Douyin in China and runs as a separate app there.

questions.question: What does "RAM" stand for?
questions.fact: RAM is wiped when you switch off your computer; storage like an SSD keeps your files.

questions.question: What is "phishing"?
options: Tricking people into giving personal data
questions.fact: Phishing is thought to be spelled with "ph" after "phone phreaks", early hackers who played with phone systems.

questions.question: What does "LED" stand for?
questions.fact: LEDs use far less electricity than old light bulbs and can last 25 times longer or more.

questions.question: Which company's famous slogan was "Think Different"?
questions.fact: "Think Different" ran from 1997 with photos of famous people like Einstein and Picasso.

questions.question: In which year was Google founded?
questions.fact: Google was founded in 1998 by Larry Page and Sergey Brin, two students at Stanford University.

questions.question: Which Nokia phone is famous for being almost indestructible?
questions.fact: The Nokia 3310 came out in 2000 and sold over 100 million units. Its game "Snake" was a huge hit.

questions.question: What is Bluetooth mainly used for?
questions.fact: Bluetooth's logo combines the old Nordic runes for King Harald's initials, H and B.

questions.question: Bluetooth is named after a Viking king of which country?
questions.fact: King Harald "Bluetooth" Gormsson is said to have united Denmark and Norway in the 900s, a bit like Bluetooth unites devices.

questions.question: What does "SIM" in SIM card stand for?
questions.fact: SIM cards have shrunk over the years, and many phones now use eSIMs with no physical card at all.

questions.question: Which company created ChatGPT?
questions.fact: ChatGPT launched in November 2022 and reached 100 million users faster than almost any app before it.

questions.question: Which tech company's name comes from a very large number?
questions.fact: A "googol" is 1 followed by 100 zeros. Google's name is a play on that word.

questions.question: What is the usual keyboard shortcut to copy on Windows?
questions.fact: Copy and paste was developed at Xerox's research lab in the 1970s.

questions.question: What does Ctrl + Z usually do?
questions.fact: Ctrl + Y or Ctrl + Shift + Z usually redoes what you just undid.

questions.question: What is a pixel?
options: A tiny dot that makes up a screen image
questions.fact: A 4K TV screen has over 8 million pixels.

questions.question: What does "4K" refer to on a TV?
questions.fact: 4K means about 4,000 pixels across. A 4K screen has four times as many pixels as Full HD.

questions.question: Which company makes the Chromecast?
questions.fact: The first Chromecast came out in 2013. Your TV is running this game on one right now!

questions.question: In which year did Netflix start streaming films online?
questions.fact: Netflix started in 1997 by posting DVDs to people's homes, and only began streaming in 2007.

questions.question: What is "app" short for?
questions.fact: Apple's App Store opened in 2008 with about 500 apps. Now there are millions.

questions.question: What is harmful software, like viruses, called in general?
questions.fact: Brain, often called the first PC virus, was made in Pakistan in 1986 by two brothers.

questions.question: What does "Ctrl + V" usually do?
questions.fact: Z, X, C and V sit side by side on the keyboard, which is why undo, cut, copy and paste got those keys.
